proposed_core_edits.name: NuT

proposed.name: NuT
proposed.def: For \(T\ge T_0\) with \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\ge u_0\), put \(\delta_T=\Delta(u_{\mathrm p}(T))\) and \(q_T=q(u_{\mathrm p}(T))\). For every integer \(j\) such that \(j\delta_T\in[0,T]\) and the level-\(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\) translate of \(A_u\) occurs at \(j\delta_T\), let \(r_T(j)=\inf\{r>j:D((r+\ell)\delta_T)\le u_{\mathrm p}(T)\text{ for }\ell=0,\ldots,q_T-1\}\). If \(r_T(j)<\infty\), then \(\mathcal N_T\) puts one point at \(\bigl(j\delta_T/T,\{\max_{j\le k<r_T(j)}D(k\delta_T)-b(T)\}/a(T)\bigr)\); if \(r_T(j)=\infty\), that root contributes no point. Thus the mark is the maximum of the forward runs-declustered pilot cluster, not the value at its first root.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The asserted peak-mark Poisson intensity requires cluster maxima. The existing symbol instead marks the first grid root above the pilot level; under the same fine-mesh continuity needed for grid approximation, that root mark remains near the pilot level and drifts downward after normalization.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A theorem for the frozen learner requires a fully specified sample map: a kernel, boundary moment system, density-normalization map, and output on singular empirical Gram matrices.
open_obligations.obstruction: The symbol for the nuisance learner names a family of boundary-corrected local-polynomial procedures rather than one measurable estimator. Uniform inverse and derivative bounds therefore cannot be asserted for the named object itself.
open_obligations.attempted: The boundary dimension, bias, stochastic term, derivative cost, both exponents, and stability of quotient and integration operations were derived for every regular complete implementation satisfying explicit moment-matrix conditions.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Put \(D=d+1\).  For a completely specified boundary local-polynomial estimator whose kernel is bounded and compactly supported, whose polynomial degree is at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), whose population boundary moment matrices have a common positive eigenvalue lower bound, and whose empirical singular-matrix convention is declared, Taylor expansion and a uniform Bernstein bound give, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \left\|\partial_a^j\widehat h_k-\partial_a^j h\right\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(h_n^{s-j}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D+2j}}}\right).
\]
At \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\), the stochastic term is the slower term.  Thus
\[
 \|\widehat h_k-h\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad \beta=\frac12-\frac{d+1}{4s},
\]
and
\[
 \|\partial_a\widehat m_k-\partial_a m\|_\infty
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
 \qquad \beta_1=\frac12-\frac{d+3}{4s}.
\]
The model restriction \(s>3(d+1)\) implies
\[
 \beta>\frac12-\frac1{12}=\frac5{12},
 \qquad
 \beta_1>\frac12-\frac{d+3}{12(d+1)}>0.
\]
The lower density bounds in \(\texttt{ass:p-bounds}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\) make division locally Lipschitz on the relevant range, and integration over the unit covariate cube is a contraction in the supremum norm.  Hence quotient formation and the displayed marginal integration preserve these orders.  This calculation proves the advertised exponents for every implementation satisfying the stated regularity properties.  It is not yet a theorem about \(\widehat\eta\): the frozen description does not select a kernel, write the boundary moment equations or normalization map, or declare the estimator on a singular empirical Gram matrix, so it does not specify a unique sample map to which the probability assertion can be applied.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform fold-conditional bound for the fitted validation-fold V-statistic and the implication from the four numerical remainders to optimized constrained-versus-unconstrained LR stability remain unproved.
open_obligations.obstruction: The within-fold empirical marginalization is a dependent V-statistic, while optimized-value comparison also needs common contact localization and slope envelopes that are not clauses of the transfer condition.
open_obligations.attempted: The product-bias, variance plug-in, and spatial-volume plug-in orders were proved. A Hoeffding decomposition now also gives the required polynomial scale for the pure bounded marginalization term, but uniformity for the fitted random kernel and optimized-value localization do not follow from that calculation.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on the zeroth-order bounds displayed in \(\texttt{lem:learner-rates}\), the definition of \(\mathfrak B_n\) gives
\[
 \mathfrak B_n=O_P(n^{-2\beta}\log n),
\]
and consequently
\[
 n^{5/6}(\log n)^{3/2}\mathfrak B_n
 =O_P\!\left(n^{5/6-2\beta}(\log n)^{5/2}\right)=o_P(1),
 \qquad
 \frac56-2\beta=-\frac16+\frac{d+1}{2s}<0.
\]
Stable product, quotient, and integration inequalities similarly give
\[
 \mathfrak K_n=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n})
\]
and
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathcal V}_n}{\mathcal V(P)}-1\right|
 =O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}
              +n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right).
\]
There is also polynomial slack in the validation-fold marginalization term.  To see its scale, fix one fold of size \(N\asymp n\), a bounded \(C^1\) function \(\phi\), and an interval \(I=(v_0,v_1]\) of length \(h\).  The off-diagonal part of
\[
 \frac1{N^2}\sum_{i,j=1}^N
 \mathbf 1\{A_i\in I\}
 \left[\phi(A_i,W_j)-\int\phi(A_i,w)p(w)\,dw\right]
\]
has a Hoeffding projection in its second argument of magnitude \(O(h)\), a zero projection in its first argument, and a degenerate kernel with second moment \(O(h)\).  Independence of distinct observations and the design-density upper bound therefore give stochastic order
\[
 O_P\!\left(\frac{h}{\sqrt n}+\frac{\sqrt h}{n}\right),
\]
while the diagonal is \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  At \(h=H_n=n^{-1/3}(\log n)^2\), multiplication by \(n^{2/3}\sqrt{\log n}\) still gives \(o_P(1)\).  This establishes the pointwise scale of the pure marginalization term, but a uniform interval inequality with the fitted random kernel and all diagonal and nuisance-residual terms remains to be supplied.  More importantly, the four scalar clauses defining \(\mathsf G_n\) do not themselves state common contact localization or slope envelopes for the two optimized isotonic problems.  A direct integration-by-parts comparison consequently stops at uncontrolled boundary and total-variation terms.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A separable locally bounded version and a quantitative common contact-radius tail over every compact set of constraint locations have not been constructed.
open_obligations.obstruction: Parabolic drift localizes individual variational pictures, but an argmin tail does not control every remote supporting chord for both one-sided constrained GCMs uniformly over a continuum. The target also does not quantify the tail strength it calls sufficient.
open_obligations.attempted: Brownian translation and affine GCM equivariance prove exact finite-dimensional stationarity. Attempts to upgrade an individual argmin bound stop at the uncontrolled remote-chord event.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Whenever the two GCM energies are defined, their finite-dimensional stationarity is exact.  For \(x,t\in\mathbb R\), set
\[
 \mathbb W_x(t)=\mathbb W(x+t)-\mathbb W(x).
\]
Then
\[
 X(x+t)-X(x)-2xt=\mathbb W_x(t)+t^2.
\]
Affine equivariance of greatest convex minorants and the change of variable \(s=x+t\) therefore give
\[
 D(x)=\Phi(\mathbb W_x),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the origin-constrained Brownian--GCM energy.  Stationarity of Brownian increments yields, for every \(m\ge1\), every \(x_1,\ldots,x_m,h\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 (\mathbb W_{x_1+h},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m+h})
 \stackrel{d}{=}
 (\mathbb W_{x_1},\ldots,\mathbb W_{x_m}),
\]
and hence translation invariance of the finite-dimensional distributions of \(D\).  This argument neither constructs a separable locally bounded modification nor bounds the joint contact radius over a continuum of constraint locations.  In particular, an individual argmin tail does not rule out a remote supporting chord that changes one of the two one-sided constrained GCMs.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The infinite-domain small-noise theorem, sharp one-cluster expansion, additive tail ratio, positive runs intensity, uniform rare-block law, anticlustering, Poisson/Gumbel limit, and growing-window padding and grid approximation remain unproved. In addition, the current marked process records root height rather than cluster maximum and requires the proposed construction correction.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact Brownian scaling and a variational action bound yield neither an infinite-domain large-deviation principle nor the translation-mode prefactor and additive constant. Long-range truncation would not prove short-range anticlustering. The current root-height mark is not the peak mark required by the asserted intensity measure.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact small-noise scaling, Hilbert-projection action lower bound, explicit finite-energy plateau witness, and prescribed finite-window PAVA reproduction were completed. The draft and named published comparators contain no theorem that supplies the missing sharp Brownian--GCM excursion analysis.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\Phi(h)\) denote the origin-constrained LR energy obtained from \(t^2+h(t)\), where \(h\) is absolutely continuous and \(h'\in L^2(\mathbb R)\).  For \(b>0\), set \(h_b(t)=b^2h(t/b)\).  Spatial and affine equivariance of the constrained and unrestricted GCMs give
\[
 \Phi(h_b)=b^3\Phi(h),
 \qquad
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h_b'(t)^2\,dt
 =b^3\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt.
\]
Brownian scaling with \(b=u^{1/3}\) thus gives the exact identity
\[
 \Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}.
\]
Define the variational action
\[
 I_\star=\inf\left\{\frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt:
                         \Phi(h)\ge1\right\}.
\]
On a finite interval containing the contact set, let \(\mathcal C_0\subset\mathcal C\) be the zero-constrained and unrestricted monotone-slope cones.  Since the baseline slope \(2t\) belongs to \(\mathcal C_0\), the Hilbert projection identity implies
\[
 \Phi(h)
 =\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C_0)
  -\operatorname{dist}^2(2t+h',\mathcal C)
 \le \|h'\|_2^2,
\]
so \(I_\star\ge1/2\).  Conversely, put \(k=4^{1/3}\), \(a=k/4\), and
\[
 h'(t)=(k-2t)\mathbf 1\{-a\le t\le k/2\}.
\]
Then \(2t+h'(t)\) is nondecreasing and equals \(k\) on \([-a,k/2]\).  Its zero-constrained projection replaces the plateau by zero on \([-a,0]\), while its unrestricted projection leaves it unchanged.  Therefore
\[
 \Phi(h)=ak^2=\frac{k^3}{4}=1,
 \qquad
 \frac12\int_{\mathbb R}h'(t)^2\,dt
 =\frac{(k+2a)^3}{12}=\frac98,
\]
and
\[
 \frac12\le I_\star\le\frac98.
\]
The prescribed finite-window PAVA calculation reproduces this localized witness, but neither Brownian scaling nor the action bracket is an infinite-domain large-deviation principle.  Even a logarithmic large-deviation limit would not determine the additive tail ratio, the translation-mode prefactor, the constant term, anticlustering, or the grid error.

There is an additional construction-level obstruction to the marked-process clause.  The present \(\mathcal N_T\) marks a pilot-level run root by the value of \(D\) at that root.  It does not mark the maximum over the cluster initiated by the root.  Under the local continuity and mesh control that the asserted grid approximation itself would require, the immediately preceding mesh value is at most \(u_{\mathrm p}(T)\), so the root overshoot is controlled by the modulus over one mesh cell.  Thus its normalized mark is of the form
\[
 \frac{D(j\Delta)-b(T)}{a(T)}
 =-h(T)+\frac{D(j\Delta)-u_{\mathrm p}(T)}{a(T)},
\]
not the normalized cluster maximum.  Since \(h(T)\to\infty\), this cannot be identified with the asserted nondegenerate peak-mark law without an additional, and contrary, root-overshoot theorem.  The natural repair is to mark each pilot root by the maximum over its forward runs-declustered cluster; that repair is proposed separately and still leaves the sharp excursion theorem to prove.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A measurable uniform coupling of the growing-domain oracle continuum LR statistic to the canonical maximum, followed by optimized cross-fitted stability, remains unavailable.
open_obligations.obstruction: The claim requires a sorted-residual strong approximation, rank and variance-clock interpolation, common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, locally uniform coefficient freezing with overlap gluing, and empirical dose-cell comparison at a moving logarithmic threshold.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact local cube-root rescaling and its spatial-volume integral were proved. A global quadratic approximation is invalid because coefficients can only be frozen on local windows, and no uniform gluing estimate is available.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For \(a\in J\), define
\[
 h_n(a)=\left\{\frac{4\kappa(a)}{n f(a)\theta'(a)^2}\right\}^{1/3}.
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\) and \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\),
\[
 c_g\le f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw\le C_g.
\]
Using \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\) and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\), direct algebra gives
\[
 \frac1{h_n(a)}
 =n^{1/3}\left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3},
 \qquad
 \int_J\frac{da}{h_n(a)}=T_n(P),
\]
and bounds \(n^{1/3}h_n(a)\) above and away from zero uniformly in \(a\in J\) and \(P\in\mathcal M\).  Hence
\[
 a\longmapsto \int_{\inf J}^{a}h_n(v)^{-1}\,dv
\]
is a bi-Lipschitz canonical coordinate and maps \(J\) to an interval of length exactly \(T_n(P)\).  This proves the spatial-volume formula, but not a coupling.  Such a coupling still requires a sorted-residual strong approximation, interpolation of the empirical rank and variance clocks, common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, local coefficient freezing with overlap gluing, and comparison of both one-sided limits in every empirical dose cell at a threshold of order \(\log n\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: Nominal calibration remains conditional on the unresolved uniform clock plug-in theorem, canonical Gumbel law, observed-law transfer, random-horizon padded-grid approximation, and quantile anti-concentration.
open_obligations.obstruction: Relative clock consistency controls substitution into a known centering and scale but cannot create the missing limiting law or identify finite padded-simulation quantiles with continuum quantiles.
open_obligations.attempted: The uniform positive volume lower bound, inverse-centering mean-value expansion, scale substitution, and conditional empirical-distribution error for the prescribed number of simulations were derived.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\texttt{ass:p-normalization}\), \(\texttt{ass:overlap}\), \(\texttt{ass:strict-slope}\), and \(\texttt{ass:variance}\) imply
\[
 \mathcal V(P)
 \ge |J|\left\{\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right\}^{1/3}>0.
\]
Consequently \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\to\infty\).  If the unresolved plug-in argument supplies
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)=1+o_P(1)
\]
uniformly, then \(\log\{\widehat T_n/T_n(P)\}=o_P(1)\) and \(\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\) uniformly.  On this event, the mean-value theorem applied to \(\mathcal E_\star(b(T))=\log T\) gives
\[
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(\widetilde b_n)}
   \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1),
\]
where \(\widetilde b_n\) lies between the two centerings.  Since
\[
 \mathcal E_\star'(u)=\beta_\star+\frac{\gamma_\star}{u}
\]
and both centerings diverge,
\[
 \frac{a(\widehat T_n)}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
        {\mathcal E_\star'(b(\widehat T_n))}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Thus an established uniform Gumbel law would pass to the analytic plug-in critical value by Slutsky's theorem.  Conditionally on the data, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality for \(n^2\) independent simulated maxima gives empirical-distribution error \(O_P(n^{-1})\).  It does not supply the unresolved padded-grid approximation, random-horizon uniformity, or limiting anti-concentration needed to turn that empirical bound into valid continuum quantiles.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The deterministic interval and threshold-crossing inversion is complete, but its nominal limiting coverage is exactly the unresolved probability assertion in feasible calibration.
open_obligations.obstruction: Convexity and set-image arguments preserve the coverage of the common LR event; they cannot prove that the proposed critical value makes that event have limiting probability one minus the nominal error.
open_obligations.attempted: The constrained value function was shown convex, the band event was identified exactly with the supremum event, and the true monotone curve was mapped to its threshold crossing under every stated convention.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For fixed \(k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define
\[
 L_k(t)=\min_{u\in\mathcal C_n,\,u_k=t}
          \sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-u_i)^2.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains \(t\mathbf 1\).  If \(u^{(1)}\) and \(u^{(2)}\) are feasible at \(t_1\) and \(t_2\), then for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \lambda u^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)u^{(2)}\in\mathcal C_n,
 \qquad
 [\lambda u^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)u^{(2)}]_k
 =\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2.
\]
Convexity of squared loss and passage to infima show that \(L_k\) is convex.  Therefore
\[
 Q_n(a,t)=L_{k(a)}(t)
 -\min_{u\in\mathcal C_n}\sum_{i=1}^n(Z_{(i)}-u_i)^2
\]
is convex in \(t\), and each sublevel set \(\mathcal C_n(a)\) is an interval, allowing the empty interval and \(\mathbb R\).  Positivity of \(\widehat\kappa\) gives the exact event identity
\[
 \{\theta(a)\in\mathcal C_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in J\}
 =\left\{\sup_{a\in J}
          \frac{Q_n(a,\theta(a))}{\widehat\kappa(a)}
          \le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\right\}
 =\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
On this event, \(\theta\) is an admissible nondecreasing selector by \(\texttt{ass:monotone}\), so the image construction in \(\texttt{def:crossing-set}\) contains its threshold crossing \(\tau_\zeta\), including the stated empty-set and endpoint conventions.  This proves that inversion loses no coverage relative to the common LR event.  It cannot establish that this event has limiting probability \(1-\alpha\), which is precisely the unresolved calibration claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The constant-coefficient clock and fixed-location identities are proved, but the proposition's invocation of the three growing-domain inference theorems cannot be certified while those theorems remain open.
open_obligations.obstruction: Constant-coefficient substitution determines the canonical interval length and fixed-origin functional but supplies no excursion, observed-law transfer, or feasible calibration theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: The spatial integral was evaluated exactly, the canonical coordinate was shown affine, and translation of a single constraint location to the origin was checked.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Suppose \(f(a)=f_0\), \(\theta'(a)=r_0\), and \(\kappa(a)=\kappa_0\) on \(J\).  Substitution into \(\texttt{def:spatial-clock}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal V(P)=|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3},
 \qquad
 T_n(P)=n^{1/3}|J|\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
The canonical coordinate has constant derivative
\[
 n^{1/3}\left(\frac{f_0r_0^2}{4\kappa_0}\right)^{1/3}
\]
and therefore maps \(J\) affinely to an interval of exactly the displayed length.  At a single fixed dose, translation places the constraint at the origin, and \(\texttt{def:canonical-field}\) gives the marginal functional \(D(0)\).  These are exact reductions.  They do not supply the growing-domain excursion theorem, the observed-law coupling, or feasible calibration invoked by the remainder of the proposition.
